Priya suspected the sensor, but the calibration logs looked perfectly normal. On the fifth attempt they swapped the cable and recorded every reading by hand. It was only when the heating clicked on that someone noticed the pattern. The room temperature, not the equipment, had been changing the results all along. They moved the rig away from the radiator and the drift disappeared completely.

The train left the station twelve minutes late, which surprised nobody on board. Outside the window, fields of wet grass gave way to a grey line of hills. A conductor walked the length of the carriage, checking tickets and apologising. Somewhere near the middle of the journey, the lights flickered and went out. Then a child laughed, someone switched on a torch, and the tension broke.

For a moment the only sound was the rattle of the wheels beneath the floor. Then a child laughed, someone switched on a torch, and the tension broke. When the power returned, the passengers were talking to each other like old friends.

Every spring she promised herself that this would be the year the garden behaved. The roses were pruned, the beds were weeded, and the fence was painted green. By June the slugs had eaten the lettuces and the mint had swallowed the path. A fox had dug a neat tunnel under the shed and seemed to be living there happily. She considered fighting back, then sat down with a cup of tea and watched instead.
